name: senses
comment: The Prism's senses (app/src/PrismSenses.lex.tex) held to the W3C Semantic Sensor Network Ontology (SOSA/SSN, Recommendation 19 October 2017). 'ontology' pins sosa.ttl as W3C serves it; PrismSosaTable and ST-01's requirements for w3c-sosa-ssn are written from it (generators/standards). 'tests' lists the Recommendation's own example graphs this slice reads, each pinned by SHA-256 as W3C serves it under 'base', with the answer of 'check': 'conforms' and the number of triples, or the first refusal. A graph is refused when it is not Turtle, when it uses a term in the SOSA namespace that SOSA does not define, or when it uses a SOSA term against its declared kind (a class as a property, a datatype property with a resource, an object property with a literal). Eight of the Recommendation's examples are refused on those grounds (unbound prefix, a stray statement, sosa:hasSimplResult, sosa:actuationMadeBy, sosa:hasProperty, sosa:resultTime given a time:Instant): the ontology is the normative text and the examples are informative, so the ontology wins. What is Turtle and how many triples a graph has were cross-checked with an independent reader (rdflib 7.6.0) when this file was written. 'examples' carries those exact bytes as the guest's acceptance vectors after the verb line 'check', then the senses: 'observe' answers the person's circumstances at a prompt as sosa:Observation s in N-Triples and 'flat' the same rows one per line; their field values are the examples of RFC 3339 (5.8), RFC 5545 (3.6.1), RFC 5870 (1, 6.1) and FIPS 180-4's SHA-256 test vectors, and every 'observe' answer passes this same 'check' before it is given. Not read yet: Turtle collections and local-name escapes, IRI dot segments, the SSN terms beyond SOSA, and om-20.ttl and dht22.ttl, which are larger than a request.
